clinician.final_diagnosis: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) with cortical and subcortical glioneuronal tubers and subependymal glial nodules
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-year-old female with intellectual disability presented to dentistry hospital with dental caries and tooth pain. Clinical history revealed seizures managed with Carbamazepine and Phenobarbital, and wart-like facial lesions beginning at age 7. Physical examination documented facial angiofibromas with butterfly distribution over the nose (starting age 7, largest 0.5 cm), hypomelanotic macules (ash-leaf spots, 2×2 cm on back), and fibromatous lesions in hair folds (1×1×1 cm, popular, sessile, firm). Brain MRI and CT imaging confirmed multiple cortical and subcortical tubers and subependymal glial nodules, with intact neurologic examination and no giant cell astrocytomas or aneurysms. Systemic screening excluded cardiac rhabdomyomas, renal angiomyolipomas, and other major organ involvement. Dental panoramic radiography revealed hypoplastic enamel and poor oral hygiene with multiple teeth requiring endodontic treatment. Laboratory tests were normal. The constellation of clinical, dermatologic, and neuroimaging findings established the diagnosis of tuberous sclerosis complex.
